result.question: We have a rule for Transformer 1 at MAIN: if it reaches IEEE C57.104 Condition 3, we plan an outage and go to monthly oil sampling. Check whether we're there. Work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630. If it's Condition 3 or 4, do the following. Look at the MAIN schedule for the 21 days after the latest sample date and propose the 2-day outage window with the fewest scheduled work orders. Create a priority 1 outage and inspection work order for that window, with a note to notify the manufacturer. Create a separate work order for the next monthly DGA sample, dated 30 days after the latest sample. If it's Condition 2, don't plan an outage. Just create a quarterly resample work order. If it's Condition 1, create nothing and tell me how many ppm of headroom we have to 1921. In every case, first check for open work orders on Transformer 1 that already cover an outage or DGA sampling, and don't duplicate them. If one exists, reference it and explain how your recommendation differs. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.
result.answer:
Yes, you're past the trigger. Transformer 1 is at **Condition 4**, not just Condition 3. I created the outage work order, but not the monthly DGA work order, because an open DGA work order already exists.

**TDCG from the latest oil sample (2024-01-19)**
- Hydrogen: 2,850 ppm
- Methane: 7,400 ppm
- Ethane: 5,470 ppm
- Ethylene: 16,650 ppm
- Acetylene: 7 ppm
- CO: 32 ppm
- **Total: 32,409 ppm.** That is more than 4630, so it's Condition 4 (about 7 times the limit).

None of the six gases was null, so nothing was carried forward.

**Open work orders already on Transformer 1**
- **1000052:** a confirmatory DGA oil sample, priority 1, awaiting approval, with no date.
- **1000051:** an on-load tap changer (OLTC) inspection, priority 1, awaiting approval. It isn't an outage work order.

**Outage: created WO 1000053**
- It's a priority 1 outage and inspection for **2024-01-20 to 2024-01-21**.
- No work orders are scheduled at MAIN anywhere from 2024-01-20 to 2024-02-09, so every 2-day window tied at zero. I picked the earliest one.
- Its notes say to notify the manufacturer and to do the OLTC inspection (1000051) during the same outage. 1000051 targets a start of 2024-01-19 and doesn't plan an outage, so 1000053 adds the de-energized window and full internal inspection.
- The work order tool couldn't auto-number it, so I set the number to 1000053 by hand. I also shortened its title because the tool cut the first version off.

**Monthly DGA sample: not created**
1000052 already covers DGA sampling on this transformer, so I didn't add a duplicate. My recommendation differs from it in two ways:
- 1000052 is a single sample with no date, based on a forecast of 32,306 ppm.
- The rule calls for ongoing monthly sampling, with the next sample dated **2024-02-18** (30 days after the latest sample).

One option is to add that date and the monthly frequency to 1000052's notes. Or, if you see the monthly sample as a separate job, I can create it as its own work order.

Everything is dated early 2024 because the latest oil sample is from 2024-01-19, more than two years old. You'll probably want to move these dates to current ones before approving.
